name: Rotating Assembly
description: Crankshaft, rods, pistons, rings, pins, bearings, reluctor and crank sprocket - the parts that make the engine survive sustained high-rpm, high-g road racing.

components.name: Crankshaft
components.description: Forged steel crankshaft with 2.559 in mains and 2.100 in rod journals, 8-bolt rear flange and a pressed-on 58X reluctor ring. The LT4 forged 1538MV crank is a robust baseline; race builds go to 4340 billet/forged cranks (Callies, Manley, etc.) mainly for strokers.
components.location: Bottom of the block on the main bearings, centerline about y = 0.40 m.

factory.name: GM LT4 forged 1538MV crankshaft (wet sump)
factory.notes: Dry-sump LT4 crank 12674743. LT1 cranks: 12623492 (wet), 12629940 (dry). Wet and dry sump cranks differ at the snout/oil pump drive and balancer bolt.

raceOptions.name: 4340 forged/billet LT crank (stroker 4.000 in common)
raceOptions.notes: Use a 58X reluctor and Gen V snout; verify oil pump drive (wet vs dry sump) and squirter clearance. Part numbers not verified here.

specs.End play: Set at #3 thrust; typical 0.004-0.008 in (estimate - verify GM spec)

installNotes: Clean every oil passage with brushes; inspect journals for scoring.
Lay in the upper main shells with assembly lube on the faces, set the crank, install caps per engine.block.main-caps.
Measure end play with a dial indicator after torquing.
Balance the crank with the actual rods/pistons/pins/rings/bearings (bobweight) if any rotating parts are changed.
inspection: Magnaflux at each rebuild; check journals for size/taper.

components.name: Connecting rods & rod bolts
components.description: Factory LT rods are 6.098 in powdered-metal I-beam rods with M9 x 1 x 43 torque-to-yield bolts. For a road-race build with sustained high rpm and boost, forged 4340 H-beam or I-beam rods with ARP fasteners are the usual upgrade.
components.location: Between each piston wrist pin and its crank rod journal; two rods share each crank throw (left/right bank).

factory.name: GM powdered-metal I-beam rod, 6.098 in
factory.notes: LT1 rod 12654242; current service rod for 6.2L LT1/L86/L87/LT2 listed as 12714549. 2.225 in big-end housing bore.

raceOptions.name: Texas Speed LS/LT Super H-Beam 6.125 in forged 4340 rods
Texas Speed LT1/L86/L87 drop-in forged piston & rod set (JE flat-top + TSP H-beam)
raceOptions.notes: Drop-in with stock crank, no balance listed.

raceOptions.name: Carrillo / Manley / Callies Ultra rods (custom LT length)
raceOptions.notes: Torque/stretch per rod card. Part numbers not verified here.

hardware.torqueSequence: Alternate bolts: both to 15 ft-lb, then each +85°.
hardware.threadlocker: Clean engine oil on threads and under head
hardware.notes: Summit LT1 & LT4 tables and Michigan Motorsports all list 15 ft-lb + 85°.

hardware.item: Aftermarket rod bolt (ARP 2000 / L19 / Custom Age 625+)
hardware.torque: Per rod card - torque to the specified stretch (commonly ~0.0055-0.0065 in for 7/16 ARP 2000)
hardware.torqueSequence: Lube with ARP Ultra-Torque, torque in 3 steps, verify each bolt with a stretch gauge.
hardware.reuse: Inspect - replace if stretch exceeds limit
hardware.notes: ARP advises using the rod manufacturer’s specification; stretch method preferred.

installNotes: Size big ends with bolts at final torque; mark rod/cap pairs.
Fit rod bolt protectors over the bolts when inserting the piston/rod to protect the journal.
Check side clearance with feeler gauges for each pair.
Chamfered side of the big end faces the crank cheek (radius).
inspection: At rebuild: check bolt stretch, big-end roundness, small-end bushing wear.

components.name: Pistons
components.description: LT4 uses forged aluminum flat-top pistons with valve and DI-injector reliefs (about 10:1 CR); LT1 uses cast hypereutectic domed pistons (11.5:1). Race builds use forged 2618/4032 pistons sized for the boost level and the DI spray pattern (or port-injection).
components.location: In each cylinder bore, attached to the rod by the wrist pin.

factory.name: GM LT4 forged aluminum flat-top piston, 11 cc net volume
factory.notes: LT1: hypereutectic cast, domed, 0.6 cc net volume. Pins 0.9431 in full floating (LT4 pin DLC-coated steel).

raceOptions.name: Manley Gen V LT forged pistons 560465C-8
raceOptions.notes: 4.065 bore, for 4.000 stroke / 6.125 rod stroker; 9.8:1 with LT4 65.5 cc heads.

raceOptions.name: JE / Wiseco / Diamond / Mahle forged LT pistons
raceOptions.notes: Specify DI injector notch (or none for port-injection conversion), valve reliefs for cam/limiter combination, and pin height for rod length.

specs.Valve reliefs: Required for intake/exhaust plus DI injector relief

installNotes: Orient per the arrow/notch (toward front) and DI relief toward the injector side.
Use a tapered ring compressor (e.g. BTR 4.075 in tool) and tap in with a hammer handle.
Check piston-to-valve clearance with clay when using a non-stock cam or phaser limiter (minimum ~0.080 in intake / 0.100 in exhaust typical).
Check deck clearance (piston to deck at TDC).
inspection: Borescope crowns between events for detonation pitting/erosion near the ring lands.

components.name: Piston rings
components.description: Three-ring pack per piston: top compression ring, second ring and three-piece oil ring. LT4 factory top ring is PVD-coated steel, second ring chrome, oil ring nitrided stainless. Ring end gaps must be file-fit to the boost/nitrous level.

factory.name: GM LT4 ring set (PVD top / chrome 2nd / nitrided oil)
factory.notes: Service replacements: Hastings 2M5381 (LT1/L86/L87 stock), 2N5295 (LT4 / L8T nitride top).

raceOptions.name: Total Seal / Mahle file-fit race ring packs

specs.Top ring gap (boosted, guideline): about 0.0055 x bore (~0.022 in) - follow piston/ring maker (estimate)

installNotes: File-fit each ring in its own bore, square with a piston, measure gap with feeler gauge.
Stagger gaps per manufacturer (never aligned, keep away from pin bores/thrust faces).
Install with a ring expander; "dot/pip" up.
inspection: Leak-down test; blow-by into the catch can is a trend indicator.

components.name: Wrist pins & pin retainers
components.description: Full-floating 0.9431 in wrist pins (LT4: DLC-coated steel) retained by locks in the piston pin bores. Aftermarket forged pistons usually come with tool-steel pins and round-wire or spiral locks.
components.location: Through the piston pin bosses and the rod small end.

factory.name: GM 0.9431 in full-floating pin (DLC coated on LT4)

raceOptions.name: Tool-steel / DLC pins supplied with forged pistons
raceOptions.notes: Match pin wall thickness to boost level.

installNotes: Oil pins, check pin-to-bore clearance, fully seat both locks and rotate them to confirm seating.

components.name: Connecting rod bearings
components.description: Rod bearing shell pairs for the 2.100 in rod journals. Road-race engines with long high-g sessions are hard on rod bearings; use a coated, harder race bearing and keep oil pressure/temperature under control.
components.location: Rod big ends on the crank rod journals.

factory.name: GM Gen V rod bearings
factory.notes: GM 12656817 listed for 2014-2016 LT1/L86/LT4; 12735504 for later 6.2L LT1/L86/L87 and 6.6L L8T.

raceOptions.name: King XP rod bearings, std (Gen V LT)
King XP coated rod bearings (Gen V LT)

installNotes: Install shells dry in the rod/cap, lube faces; measure clearance at final rod bolt torque.
inspection: Cut oil filter every event; trend oil-analysis lead/copper.

components.name: 58X crankshaft reluctor wheel
components.description: 58-tooth (60-2) trigger wheel pressed onto the crankshaft; read by the crank position sensor. Must be the 58X Gen IV/V style to work with the E92 ECM or most race ECUs’ GM 58X decoder.
components.location: On the crankshaft near the rear main, inside the block.

raceOptions.name: Aftermarket crank with 58X wheel installed
raceOptions.notes: Order with 58X; confirm index position relative to TDC #1 matches GM.

installNotes: Never remove/re-press without the correct fixture - clocking must match GM.

components.name: Crankshaft timing sprocket
components.description: Steel sprocket on the crank snout that drives the timing chain; keyed to the crank. Cloyes and others offer adjustable (multi-keyway) crank sprockets for degreeing the cam.
components.location: Front of crank snout, behind the oil pump drive and front cover.

factory.name: GM Gen V crank sprocket
factory.notes: Timing mark aligns with cam phaser sprocket mark per GM procedure.

raceOptions.name: Cloyes 9-3678X5 LT timing set (adjustable steel crank gear, single-row true roller)

installNotes: Install with crank key; align timing marks (#1 TDC) before fitting the chain.
Degree the cam with a degree wheel on the crank snout before the front cover goes on.
